targets.approach: Park at the last switchback on Chimney Peak Road that leads up to Lamont Saddle, then hike west, contouring, to the rock. The main wall faces west, on the ridge immediately east of Burnt Granola. Endorphin Crack is the system of thin cracks toward the right end of the main wall.
targets.name: Endorphin Crack

targets.approach: Park at the last switchback on Chimney Peak Road that leads up to Lamont Saddle, then hike west, contouring, to the rock. The main wall faces west, on the ridge immediately east of Burnt Granola. Heavy Weather is the conspicuous wide crack at the middle of the main wall.
targets.name: Heavy Weather

targets.approach: Park at the last switchback on Chimney Peak Road that leads up to Lamont Saddle, then hike west, contouring, to the rock. The main wall faces west, on the ridge immediately east of Burnt Granola. Tradewinds begins at the wall's left end in a vertical crack and carries on up the face once the crack runs out.
targets.name: Tradewinds

targets.approach: From the May Lake or Murphy Creek trailheads it is a long walk and some overland travel to the cliff, which stands on Tuolumne Peak. Basket Case starts just right of The Last Easter Egg and follows a left-slanting crack.
targets.name: Basket Case

targets.approach: From the May Lake or Murphy Creek trailheads it is a long walk and some overland travel to the cliff, which stands on Tuolumne Peak. Shiny Metallic Purple Armor begins under the right edge of a long finger-width flake at the cliff's right end.
targets.name: Shiny Metallic Purple Armor

targets.approach: From the May Lake or Murphy Creek trailheads it is a long walk and some overland travel to the cliff, which stands on Tuolumne Peak. The Last Easter Egg begins at the middle of the cliff under a flowery groove and ramp.
targets.name: The Last Easter Egg

targets.approach: From the May Lake or Murphy Creek trailheads it is a long walk and some overland travel to the cliff, which stands on Tuolumne Peak. Thunder Bunny is on the left side of the cliff, some distance left of The Last Easter Egg, up a short buttress and the face above.
targets.name: Thunder Bunny

targets.approach: Approach Miter Basin over Cottonwood Pass, New or Old Army Pass, or Arc Pass; camping is good anywhere in the basin. The Miter is the two-headed peak between the Sky Blue Lake and Iridescent Lake basins. Janitorial Service is on the north summit; from Sky Blue Lake, go uphill eastward to the middle of its west face.
targets.descent_text: Unrope on top of the final short pitch, scramble to the summit, and descend by the Northwest Chute, which is the easiest way up or down the peak.
targets.name: Janitorial Service

targets.approach: Approach Miter Basin over Cottonwood Pass, New or Old Army Pass, or Arc Pass; camping is good anywhere in the basin. The Miter is the two-headed peak between the Sky Blue Lake and Iridescent Lake basins. The Miterhorn takes the west arete of the south summit. Head toward the long splitter corner, then traverse left around it to a pedestal that marks the foot of the arete.
targets.descent_text: After the south summit, traverse over to the true north summit and descend the Northwest Chute, which is the easiest way up or down the peak.
targets.name: The Miterhorn

targets.approach: Approach Miter Basin over Cottonwood Pass, New or Old Army Pass, or Arc Pass; camping is good anywhere in the basin. The Miter is the two-headed peak between the Sky Blue Lake and Iridescent Lake basins. The Pen is Miter than the Sword takes a direct line up the southwest face to the higher north summit, starting from discontinuous ledges and following a crack system.
targets.descent_text: Descend by the Northwest Chute, which is the easiest way up or down the peak.
targets.name: The Pen is Miter than the Sword

targets.approach: Take the Sphinx Creek Trail toward Avalanche Pass and work over to the gully on the east side of the formation. Descend that gully, a class 3-4 scramble, to a ledge close to the lowest part of the east face, where the route starts.
targets.name: Cotton Mouth Khafra

targets.approach: The crag is a buttress on the left side of the glaciated bowl under Tuolumne Peak's southeast face. It is a long cross-country trip from May Lake or from Polly Dome Lakes. Fun begins at a pair of cracks next to the arete at the right-hand limit of the climbing.
targets.descent_text: Climb or scramble off to the right.
targets.name: Fun

targets.approach: The crag is a buttress on the left side of the glaciated bowl under Tuolumne Peak's southeast face. It is a long cross-country trip from May Lake or from Polly Dome Lakes. Happy begins in the strong crack on the left wall of a dark corner that faces right.
targets.descent_text: Scramble off to the right or the left at the top.
targets.name: Happy

targets.approach: The crag is a buttress on the left side of the glaciated bowl under Tuolumne Peak's southeast face. It is a long cross-country trip from May Lake or from Polly Dome Lakes. Sadness begins beside an arete, in cracks that lead to a small pine.
targets.descent_text: Climb or scramble off to the left.
targets.name: Sadness

targets.approach: The crag is a buttress on the left side of the glaciated bowl under Tuolumne Peak's southeast face. It is a long cross-country trip from May Lake or from Polly Dome Lakes. Super begins at the left end of the crag, beside the base of some dark water streaks.
targets.descent_text: Traverse off to the left at the top.
targets.name: Super

targets.approach: The Thunderbird Wall is reached from the foot of the Claim Jumper Wall by a brief trail and some scrambling, and a similar link comes in from the neighbouring Gunsmoke Wall. The wall faces east, toward both of those walls. Sugarloaf lies downhill and to the left of High Plains Drifter, at the east face's left edge.
targets.name: Sugarloaf

targets.approach: Park in the large turnout on the south side of Highway 18 just west of the Big Bear Lake dam, then hike downhill along Bear Creek, staying west of the ridge. The short south and southwest-facing walls are close by. Dead Battery is the right-angling chimney and gully in the middle of the south face.
targets.name: Dead Battery

targets.approach: Park in the large turnout on the south side of Highway 18 just west of the Big Bear Lake dam, then hike downhill along Bear Creek, staying west of the ridge. The short south and southwest-facing walls are close by. Flat Spare Tire is a short hand crack a little right of Dead Battery.
targets.name: Flat Spare Tire

targets.approach: Park in the large turnout on the south side of Highway 18 just west of the Big Bear Lake dam, then hike downhill along Bear Creek, staying west of the ridge. The short south and southwest-facing walls are close by. Hitchhiker is a short fist crack passing a wedged block, close to Flat Spare Tire at the south face's right end.
targets.name: Hitchhiker

targets.approach: Park in the large turnout on the south side of Highway 18 just west of the Big Bear Lake dam, then hike downhill along Bear Creek, staying west of the ridge. The short south and southwest-facing walls are close by. Street Sweeper is in the center of the left wall, which faces southwest.
targets.descent_text: Belay on gear and walk off.
targets.name: Street Sweeper

targets.approach: From the Tuttle Creek trailhead, walk the old dirt road to the Ashram stone house, then continue up the North Fork of Tuttle Creek on a faint, cairned trail on the south side of the drainage. After a long stretch the cairned path comes close to the base of the slab. Leave it where it looks good and scramble straight up to the base. Jim's Buttress runs up the left margin of the big steep buttress on the canyon's south flank.
targets.descent_text: Descend the slopes on the right side (looking up) back to the approach path.
targets.name: Jim's Buttress

targets.approach: Keep climbing the Pine Creek trail until the wall shows on your left, then work up the basin below it along its right-hand side. Alpine Creek starts on the right side of the triangular slab.
targets.descent_text: Rappel Thinking Makes It So, reached by traversing left and then back right down a ramp.
targets.name: Alpine Creek

targets.approach: Keep climbing the Pine Creek trail until the wall shows on your left, then work up the basin below it along its right-hand side. Thinking Makes It So begins on a pedestal at the buttress toe, to the left of the slab.
targets.name: Thinking Makes It So

targets.approach: Keep climbing the Pine Creek trail until the wall shows on your left, then work up the basin below it along its right-hand side. This Is Water starts on the right face of the Upper Brownstone dihedral.
targets.name: This Is Water

targets.approach: Keep climbing the Pine Creek trail until the wall shows on your left, then work up the basin below it along its right-hand side. Throwback Cracks goes up the left-hand face of the big dihedral at the wall's left end.
targets.name: Throwback Cracks

targets.approach: Keep climbing the Pine Creek trail until the wall shows on your left, then work up the basin below it along its right-hand side. Unknown Upper Brownstone starts in the right-facing corner on the left side of the slabby toe.
targets.name: Unknown Upper Brownstone

targets.approach: Trapper Dome is by Courtright Reservoir. Park in one of the turnouts beside the road near the dam and walk toward the granite. At the base of the south face, follow a ramp beside a fallen dead tree up to a shelf where numerous face routes of the upper tier begin. It is the single-bolt line that finishes at the anchors shared with Claim Jumper.
targets.name: Phone Sex is Safe Sex

targets.approach: From the hairpin-turn parking area, follow the Coven trail north, down across a seasonal stream and back uphill. At the Coven, scramble up and left to the mostly flat base of the south-facing Voodoo Wall. Mary Had A Little Jam goes up the gully left of the main wall, starting left of Witch Hunt, and stems between walls to a huge block.
targets.descent_text: Finish at the lower-off anchors of Witch Hunt and lower from them.
targets.name: Mary Had A Little Jam

targets.approach: From the hairpin-turn parking area, follow the Coven trail north, down across a seasonal stream and back uphill. At the Coven, scramble up and left to the mostly flat base of the south-facing Voodoo Wall. The Witches Crook begins right beside Witch Hunt, inside the chute used to get down from Lighten My Load, at the foot of a pine.
targets.descent_text: Set up a gear anchor at the top and bring up your partner, then shift across to the Witch Hunt lower-offs and lower from those.
targets.name: The Witches Crook

targets.approach: Park in the dirt pullout west of the Tuolumne store and follow the trail up past some early granite, then through the second band of trees to the base of East Cottage Dome. Do not go up toward the summit; keep to the base, heading left, until you reach a dark wall carrying a few bolts, then scramble up easy ground to the main climbs. Ballroom Dancing is between Orange Plasma and Comfortably Numb.
targets.name: Ballroom Dancing

targets.approach: From Hunsaker Road in Running Springs, take the dirt road at the end of Cove Circle and follow the trail downhill to Deep Creek Narrows. The West Face is the wall on your right as you go down the approach gully to the creek and rock pools. Bat Crack is partway up that gully, on the right of the Androids roof.
targets.name: Bat Crack

targets.approach: Use the same parking and start as for the Hungover Wall on Keller Peak Road, then climb beyond the wall's right-hand end, go east, and take a trail up to the base of the buttress. Window to the Sky starts up and right from Windwalker, climbing an elevator-shaft chimney into twin cracks that lead to the natural window.
targets.name: Window to the Sky

targets.approach: Use the same parking and start as for the Hungover Wall on Keller Peak Road, then climb beyond the wall's right-hand end, go east, and take a trail up to the base of the buttress. Windwalker begins in a brief crack at the foot of the buttress and climbs its southeast face.
targets.name: Windwalker
